findings.title: False-clean report: any same-document navigation (history.replaceState / pushState / hash change) by the AUDITED page during its own load/settle window moves `since` forward, silently dropping the page's own console errors and broken requests from before it, while observation.coversWholeDocument stays true.
findings.reproductionRate: Controlled fixture (runtime-direct): own console.error dropped in 35/36 trials across replace/push/hash x at {sync,0,200,1000}ms; with the nav at 200ms or 1000ms, consoleErrors AND brokenRequests are both [] in 18/18 trials (page actually has 1 console.error + 2 404s). CLI: see probe-cli-false-clean.json. CLI: `audit /spa --json --fail-on-diff` (page with 1 console.error + 2 404s, replaceState at 200ms) exits 0 with consoleErrors [] and brokenRequests [] 3/3 -- a false CI pass.
findings.realWorldPrevalence: 8/10 real sites audited live (nextjs.org, react.dev, vercel.com, github.com, npmjs.com, vuejs.org, angular.dev, svelte.dev) fire 2-5 main-frame framenavigated events during the audit window (same-document router/hydration navs at +7ms..+1047ms after commit); only developer.mozilla.org and wikipedia.org fire exactly one. So `since` lands 125ms-1047ms AFTER the real document commit on most modern SPA sites -- the initial-load window where most asset 404s and hydration errors happen. (These specific popular sites happened to be near-clean, measured drop 1 console error on npmjs.com; the mechanism, not the count, is the finding.)
findings.mechanism: runtime.audit keeps its framenavigated listener attached for the whole navigate()+settleMs window and overwrites navCommittedAt on EVERY main-frame event. Puppeteer 25.5.0 FrameManager#onFrameNavigatedWithinDocument emits FrameManagerEvent.FrameNavigated for Page.navigatedWithinDocument too (FrameManager.js:406-415). computeObservation no longer min()s against documentStartedAt, so nothing bounds it.
findings.fixDirection: Record only cross-document commits (CDP Page.frameNavigated on the main frame, or ignore frames whose FrameEvent.FrameNavigatedWithinDocument fired / whose loaderId did not change); keep the LAST cross-document commit so JS redirect chains still work.

findings.title: The audited URL's own main-document HTTP error status (404/500, and a 302 -> 404 redirect) is no longer reported in brokenRequests -- the main-document 'response' event is timestamped just BEFORE framenavigated (commit), so commit-time scoping drops it. audit-1 listed 'audited URL itself 404 (reported as broken request)' as a PASSING edge case.
findings.reproductionRate: 15/15 runtime-direct (main-404 x5, main-500 at 150ms x5, 302->404 x5): brokenRequests [] every time; only Chrome's generic 'Failed to load resource' console line survives. CLI main-500: missing from brokenRequests 2/3 (exit still 1 only because Chrome logs a generic "Failed to load resource" console error).

findings.gap: GAP-261 (incomplete fix; new double-print introduced by fix-1)
findings.title: `audit --json` stdout is TWO concatenated JSON documents when a never-handled alert opens while the audit's capture phase (screenshot/evaluate) is in flight: withSession's pre-emption branch prints the blocked doc, then the ABANDONED runtime.audit() rejects ('Protocol error (Runtime.evaluate): Target closed') and fix-1's new cmdAudit catch prints a second blocked doc. JSON.parse(stdout) fails.
findings.reproductionRate: 12/18 with alert at 1500-1575ms (3 reps x 6 offsets); 2/7 in the wider 0..1800ms sweep. Outside the capture window all shapes are single-doc (see below).
findings.fixDirection: cmdAudit's catch must not print when withSession already emitted the pre-empted doc (single writer / emitted flag), or the abandoned work must be muted after pre-emption -- exactly the hazard withSession's own comment warns about.
findings.mutationNote: M8b (delete the cmdAudit catch) does not fix it: the alert-at-D11-check shape then prints nothing/exit 1 and the 1575ms shape still double-prints -- two uncoordinated writers race.

findings.title: Mutation survivors: M3 (drop the main-frame filter in the framenavigated handler) and M4 (keep FIRST event instead of LAST -- live-verified to break the JS redirect chain, reporting ja-own/jb-own of earlier documents) both pass all 193 capability-runtime tests. M8 (delete fix-1's cmdAudit dialog catch) passes all 161 cli tests; there are no CLI unit tests for any GAP-261 path. GAP-261 CLI mutations M6 (reportDialogs -> stdout), M7 (gate catch -> text lines), M9 (pre-empt doc removed) are all caught by the live probe/live-verify but by 0 unit tests.

MCP/SDK: no output corruption (0 non-JSON MCP stdout lines; every call returns a schema-valid report or a clean isError / thrown error), but an alert on load makes browser.audit/Page.audit hang 30s and fail with a misleading "Navigation timeout of 30000 ms exceeded" instead of D11's fast dialog error; an alert opening during capture makes the SDK audit return a valid report after ~31.5s (auto-dismiss) with no mention of the dialog. Not the GAP-261 class; likely pre-existing navigate()/auto-dismiss behavior.

Stale comment in runtime.ts audit() (GAP-262 block) says the commit time is still min()d against performance.timeOrigin "unchanged" -- the min() was removed. Also: sameTabHashAudit (audit url = current page + #frag) reports only post-hash activity yet coversWholeDocument:true (5/5).

Pre-existing, not FR2-12: parallel `turbo build --force` fails in @sutradhar/server (contracts dist race; --concurrency=1 OK). CLI `close` leaves the sutradhar-cli-<ts> Chrome user-data-dir in os.tmpdir(); 94 such dirs from this audit's own CLI runs were removed by the auditor (no process referenced them).

minDiagnosis: CONFIRMED. site-audit.ts computeObservation navigated branch is exactly `since = input.navCommittedAt ?? documentStartedAt;` (no min). Mutation M1 (reintroduce min against documentStartedAt) -> live core repro leaks 12-13 entries 5/5 (performance.timeOrigin ~= navigation start). Stale comment remains in runtime.ts (~line 1602) claiming the commit time is still min()d against performance.timeOrigin "unchanged" -- false, doc-only.
gap264: RA4b does exercise the commit-time boundary: M2 (commit value shifted 1s early) fails exactly RA4b (1 failed | 192 passed); M1 (min reintroduced) fails AR11(b). Sources restored, sha256 verified identical (pre-mutation-sha256.txt), package rebuilt.
sameDocResidualJudgment: NOT narrow. The disclosed residual was framed as "a same-document nav on the same tab followed by an audit" -- that exact shape is rare and mostly benign. The real exposure is the audited page itself doing replaceState/pushState/hash during load, which 8/10 real modern sites do within 7-1047ms of commit. It must be fixed before DONE (A2-F1).
